catalog_quote: Im Zimbrischen liegt der Wortakzent normalerweise auf der Stammsilbe, die in der Regel mit der ersten Silbe des Wortes zusammenfällt. Der Akzent kann jedoch auch auf andere Silben fallen, besonders bei Lehnwörtern aus dem romanischen Sprachraum (Italienisch, Trentinisch, Ladinisch usw.) und bei den Wörtern mit Präfix. Als allgemeine Richtlinie wird der Akzent nur dann graphisch dargestellt, wenn die richtige Betonung nicht sofort intuitiv zu erkennen ist. new_statements.quote: Im Zimbrischen liegt der Wortakzent normalerweise auf der Stammsilbe, die in der Regel mit der ersten Silbe des Wortes zusammenfällt. Der Akzent kann jedoch auch auf andere Silben fallen, besonders bei Lehnwörtern aus dem romanischen Sprachraum (Italienisch, Trentinisch, Ladinisch usw.) und bei den Wörtern mit Präfix. [...] wird er nicht angezeigt in Wörtern wie khriage 'Krieg', bei denen die Betonung regelmäßig auf der Stammsilbe (der ersten Silbe) liegt, oder wie gevallt 'gefallen', bei denen die Betonung des Wortstamms (vall-) in der zweiten Silbe auch regelmäßig ist, da das unbetonte Präfix ge- vorangeht. Hingegen wird der Akzent in Wörtern wie botù 'Knopf', konfì 'Grenze', frenàrn 'bremsen' angegeben.
new_statements.translation: In Cimbrian the word accent normally lies on the stem syllable, which as a rule coincides with the first syllable of the word. The accent can however also fall on other syllables, especially in loanwords from the Romance area (Italian, Trentino, Ladin etc.) and in words with a prefix. [...] it is not marked in words like khriage 'war', where the stress regularly lies on the stem syllable (the first syllable), or like gevallt 'fallen', where the stress on the word stem (vall-) in the second syllable is also regular, since the unstressed prefix ge- precedes. By contrast the accent is marked in words like botù 'button', konfì 'border', frenàrn 'to brake'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Germanic-type root stress: primary stress on the stem (root) syllable, which is word-initial in native words unless an unstressed prefix (ge-, dar-/vor-, etc.) precedes; Romance loanwords keep their non-initial (often final) stress and are the main exception. Corroborated independently for Sette Comuni Cimbrian by Martello Martalar 1974: 16 ('L'accento tonico delle parole cade normalmente all'inizio, o sulla seconda sillaba se la prima è un prefisso atono come ad esempio ga-') and by Geiser's online course (initial stress unless marked). Within diphthongs the accent is always on the first vowel (Panieri 2006: 27; Nordera 1989 for Giazza).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not treated as such. Panieri 2006: 25 says that in compounds the accent falls on the stem syllable of each element 'fast als ob es sich um zwei getrennte Wörter handelte' (spàr-héart, vòrt-gìan, àuz-béne). Kranzmayer 1981: 120 mentions in passing that four-syllable words have a 4-1-3-1 stress pattern (i.e. a secondary peak on the third syllable) and therefore behave quantitatively like disyllables.
new_statements.exceptions: Romance loanwords with non-initial stress (botù, konfì, frenàrn); words with unstressed prefixes stress the stem (gevallt, darzürnt); enclitic pronouns attach without shifting stress (i làidar, khémmenda); orthographic accent marks are used only where stress is not predictable. Bacher 1905: 213 notes Lusérn altvr 'altar' keeps MHG initial stress against Italian altàre.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (Wortakzent), citation forms and compounds; also comments on which words are atonic in the sentence (Martalar: articles, auxiliaries, personal pronouns; Kranzmayer §31 'Schwachtonige Wörter'). Sentence accent is described separately by Bacher 1905 §§94-98 as a musical/pitch pattern and by Kranzmayer 1981: 25 ('Der Satzakzent gleicht dem venezianischen, nicht dem tirolischen').
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding statement (Panieri et al. 2006) describes the Cimbrian of Lusérn (Luserna, Trentino), the only fully vital variety; Glottolog 5.1 has no separate child languoid for it under cimb1238. The corroborating Martalar 1974 statement is for Sette Comuni (Sieben Gemeinden / Roana-Asiago) Cimbrian; Geiser's online course (initial stress unless marked) also describes Sette Comuni 'classical' Cimbrian. Kranzmayer 1981 covers all three areas. All describe the same stress placement (stem/initial), so no dialect conflict.

new_statements.quote: 5) Raddolcimento della vocale radicale (nei prestiti recenti dall’italiano si raddolcisce la vocale tonica);* [...] * Per raddolcimento si intende lo spostamento articolatorio della vocale da posteriore ad anteriore: u diventa ü; o diventa ö; a e å diventano e. || I numeri cardinali da tredici a diciannove vengono formati aggiungendo all’unità il suffisso atono –tzane esempio: drai–tzane.
new_statements.translation: 5) Fronting of the root vowel (in recent loans from Italian the tonic [stressed] vowel is fronted);* [...] * By 'raddolcimento' is meant the articulatory shift of the vowel from back to front: u becomes ü; o becomes ö; a and å become e. || The cardinal numbers from thirteen to nineteen are formed by adding to the unit the unstressed suffix -tzane, e.g. drai-tzane.

new_statements.relation_note: Silent on placement. What it does contain is compatible with the existing Panieri et al. 2006 statement (stress on the stem syllable, normally the first; other syllables mainly in Romance loans): the exercise book uses the 2006 grammar's accent-mark convention for non-initial stress in loans and prefixed verbs and defers to that grammar for pronunciation. Adds nothing that would change the catalog record. Note also the listed open_url (treffan.zimbarbort.it) is dead; the live URL is https://treffan.istitutocimbro.it/home.page.
new_statements.rule_in_words: No statement of word-stress placement anywhere in the 66 pages. The work is an exercise book (eserciziario), not a grammar; its pronunciation sections (BIA MA KHÖTT: 1.2 Le vocali; 2.4 Le consonanti particolari; 2.5 assimilazione consonantica; 3.2 Le sibilanti) cover vowel and consonant quality only and explicitly refer the learner to the Grammatica (Panieri et al. 2006, p. 28 for vowels) and to the online dictionary Zimbarbort for 'la pronuncia corretta'. The words accentata/non accentata (26 tokens) all refer to strong vs. clitic pronoun forms (lessons 1, 8, 12, 13; part 2 lessons 2, 7), not to word stress. Only two marginal mentions of stress exist: lesson 4 §4.2 says that in recent Italian loans umlaut ('raddolcimento') applies to the tonic vowel, and lesson 7 §7.3 calls the teen-numeral suffix -tzane 'atono' (unstressed). Its orthographic practice (accent marks on the stressed vowel of Romance loans: bakå, konfì, botù, polmü, radjonàrn, diféndarn; and on the root vowel after unstressed prefixes bo-/dar-/vor-: bohìntarn, darléschan, vorschémen, in lesson 9 sub-page 9-2 exercise 3) is consistent with stem/first-syllable stress with marked exceptions, but no rule is stated.
new_statements.exceptions: Nothing stated as a rule; implicitly, recent Italian loans carry a tonic vowel that is not the initial root vowel (dar konfì → di konfìn, dar bånko, di medisì → di medisìn) and the accent mark is written on it; the suffix -tzane is unstressed.
new_statements.identity_note: The work describes the Cimbrian of Lusérn/Luserna (Trentino) specifically — the same variety as the catalog record — produced by the Kulturinstitut Lusérn; it is not about the Sette Comuni or Tredici Comuni varieties.

sources.note: The 'Akzent' section treats only the musical/sentence accent (pitch intervals notated with Chevé numbers; §95: in isolated words the voice falls a minor third from stressed to unstressed syllable). Historical phonology is organised as 'Vokale in betonter Silbe' (p. 164) vs 'in tieftonigen und unbetonten Silben' (p. 169) with prefixes bo-, ga-, vor-, dar- unstressed; dictionary p. 213 notes altvr 'Altar' keeps MHG initial stress. No general word-stress rule stated.
